claim: In the 440 byte-exact original named fpw_* embedded RS source payloads already proven in FACT-0347, the 16 original unsigned bytes at embedded payload indices +48 through +63 form a nondecreasing sequence in all 440. Fifty-five of those 16-byte vectors are constant, 385 have one or more increases; in every one of 440, byte positions +57 through +63 are mutually equal. There are 273 distinct 16-byte byte vectors, concatenated original 7040 bytes SHA256 69a4dc4d349e75d5d011e41ea18d9e801fad19851a7424d4b937062edfcaa295; full normalized indexed 440-row SHA256 4798483892af5369892ecf0ecdd62f1a12ad43aa7f6cfe05df36f33d7d2be6d0. In all 65 original _0/_1/_2 variant families (58 pairs, seven triples, 137 source objects), every variant has an exactly identical 16-byte slice at +48..+63 and equal total embedded-source length. Earlier matching original retail DLL evidence FACT-0274 proves the code conditionally fills a System.Int32[16] using unsigned input byte reads at relative argument offsets +48..+63 and calls SkillDataMan.GetAnmNum; this establishes compatible source index positions, not that the original resource vectors are observed execution-time argument values or represent animation durations.
